strings.name: Ai Weiwei
strings.role: Artist and documentary filmmaker · Memory, power and displacement
strings.summary: Ai Weiwei works across installation, photography, architectural collaboration and documentary film. Traditional materials and everyday objects become ways to examine cultural memory, labor and public power. Sunflower Seeds explores individuals and collectivity through handmade porcelain; earthquake investigations and refugee projects connect art with social witness. An outspoken critic of repression, he was detained in 2011 and continued international exhibitions and public debate after leaving China.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 2026-11-13. Selected milestones span 1957–2026; this is not a complete catalogue or live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Addressed cultural memory and public power through installations, moving images and socially engaged projects, sustaining an international influence on contemporary art.

strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Studied at Beijing Film Academy and Parsons School of Design in New York
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Individuals and collectivity in materials
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Sunflower Seeds uses handmade porcelain seeds to examine scale, labor and individual existence, bringing traditional craft into contemporary installation.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Art as social witness
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: From investigating the Sichuan earthquake to Human Flow, names, objects and film address public responsibility and forced migration.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Discusses censorship and AI in Brussels
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Euronews reported his Bozar conversation on On Censorship, privacy, technology and individual freedom.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Button Up! opens in Manchester
strings.timeline.event-02.text: At Aviva Studios, buttons, porcelain and reconstructed architecture examined Chinese–British relations, trade and empire; the exhibition ended in September.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Releases Human Flow
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The documentary follows refugees and displaced people across countries, examining borders, conflict and everyday life during migration.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Detained for eighty-one days
strings.timeline.event-04.text: He was taken at Beijing’s airport and held in secret detention, drawing international attention; restrictions continued after his release.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Presents Sunflower Seeds at Tate Modern
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Handmade porcelain seeds from Jingdezhen filled the Turbine Hall, placing tiny individual objects in relation to immense scale.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Investigates the Sichuan earthquake
strings.timeline.event-06.text: With volunteers he gathered names of students who died, later transforming materials, testimony and memory into artworks.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Creates Dropping a Han Dynasty Urn
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Sequential photographs record the breaking of an ancient urn, provoking questions about cultural value, destruction and contemporary art.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Returns to China from New York
strings.timeline.event-08.text: After living in the United States and encountering conceptual art, he returned to Beijing and developed publishing, art spaces and transformed traditional objects.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Enters Beijing Film Academy
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Animation studies preceded his move to the United States, where he encountered different artistic ideas and urban experiences.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Beijing
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born into poet Ai Qing’s family, he grew up amid his family’s exile; cultural memory and power later became recurring artistic concerns.
